==Development==
In January 2023, ''Black Rider'' was announced as part of GMA Network's 2023 line up.<ref>{{Cite news|title=GMA Network brightens 2023 with the grandest shows |url=https://mb.com.ph/2023/01/07/gma-network-brightens-2023-with-the-grandest-shows/ |access-date=November 8, 2023 |newspaper=[[Manila Bulletin]] |language=en}}</ref> Monti Parungao was originally announced to helm the series.<ref name=cast/> Rommel Penesa and Richard Arellano later took over as his replacement. Erwin Tagle serves as an action director.<ref name=philstar>{{cite news|title=Ruru Madrid is delivery driver turned vigilante in ''Black Rider'' |url=https://www.philstar.com/the-freeman/cebu-entertainment/2023/11/01/2308086/ruru-madrid-delivery-driver-turned-vigilante-black-rider |access-date=November 8, 2023 |newspaper=[[The Philippine Star]]}}</ref>

==Casting==
In April 2024, actress [[Jillian Ward]] made a cameo appearance as Analyn Santos, who originated from the Philippine television medical drama series ''[[Abot-Kamay na Pangarap]]''.<ref name=Jillian/>

==Production==
Principal photography commenced on July 4, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/tv/black_rider/103137/bagong-primetime-series-ni-ruru-madrid-na-black-rider-nagsimula-nang-mag-taping/story |title=Bagong primetime series ni Ruru Madrid na ''Black Rider'', nagsimula nang mag-taping |author=Ruiz, Marah |website=[[GMA Network (company)|GMA Network]] |date=July 4, 2023 |access-date=September 20, 2023}}</ref>

==Ratings==
According to [[AGB Nielsen Philippines]]' Nationwide Urban Television Audience Measurement People in Television Homes, the pilot episode of ''Black Rider'' earned a 12.1% rating.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pilot episode ng ''Black Rider'', kumasa ba sa ''Batang Quiapo''? |url=https://www.pep.ph/pepalerts/pep-troika/176977/black-rider-batang-quiapo-ratings-a4118-20231107 |access-date=November 8, 2023 |website=PEP |language=en}}</ref> The final episode scored a 15.6% rating.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pep.ph/pepalerts/pep-troika/182034/black-rider-finale-ratings-a4118-20240729 |title=''Black Rider'' finale episode, nataasan ang ''Batang Quiapo'' sa ratings  |date=July 29, 2024 |website=PEP |access-date=July 30, 2024}}</ref>

'''''Black Rider''''' is a [[Philippine television drama]] action series broadcast by [[GMA Network]]. Directed by Rommel Penesa and Richard Arellano, it stars [[Ruru Madrid]] in the title role. It premiered on November 6, 2023 on the network's Telebabad line up replacing ''[[Maging Sino Ka Man (2023 TV series)|Maging Sino Ka Man]]''. The series concluded on July 26, 2024 with a total of 188 episodes. It was replaced by ''[[Pulang Araw]]'' in its timeslot.

The series is streaming online on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLGRhcC_vtOrb9sUAfbVPcvNW796sfRI2O&si=tvRv_oEoNTj3IAmJ |title=''Black Rider'' (Full Episodes) - YouTube |website=[[YouTube]] |access-date=July 29, 2024}}</ref>

==Premise==
Elias, a motorcycle delivery driver becomes a vigilante to be known as the "Black Rider". He is set to fight a syndicate, the Golden Scorpion.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mb.com.ph/2023/10/31/ruru-madrid-returns-to-primetime-as-black-rider-on-nov-6 |title=Ruru Madrid returns to primetime as ''Black Rider'' on Nov. 6 |date=November 1, 2023 |website=[[Manila Bulletin]] |access-date=April 19, 2024}}</ref>

==Development==
In January 2023, ''Black Rider'' was announced as part of GMA Network's 2023 line up.<ref>{{Cite web|title=GMA Network brightens 2023 with the grandest shows |url=https://mb.com.ph/2023/01/07/gma-network-brightens-2023-with-the-grandest-shows/ |access-date=November 8, 2023 |website=[[Manila Bulletin]] |language=en}}</ref> Monti Parungao was originally announced to helm the series.<ref name=cast/> Rommel Penesa and Richard Arellano later took over as his replacement. Erwin Tagle serves as an action director.<ref name=philstar>{{cite web|title=Ruru Madrid is delivery driver turned vigilante in ''Black Rider'' |url=https://www.philstar.com/the-freeman/cebu-entertainment/2023/11/01/2308086/ruru-madrid-delivery-driver-turned-vigilante-black-rider |access-date=November 8, 2023 |website=[[The Philippine Star]]}}</ref>

==Casting==
In April 2024, actress [[Jillian Ward]] made a cameo appearance as Analyn Santos, who originated from the Philippine television medical drama series ''[[Abot-Kamay na Pangarap]]''.<ref name=Jillian/>

==Production==
Principal photography commenced on July 4, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gmanetwork.com/entertainment/tv/black_rider/103137/bagong-primetime-series-ni-ruru-madrid-na-black-rider-nagsimula-nang-mag-taping/story |title=Bagong primetime series ni Ruru Madrid na ''Black Rider'', nagsimula nang mag-taping |author=Ruiz, Marah |website=[[GMA Network]] |date=July 4, 2023 |access-date=September 20, 2023}}</ref>

==Ratings==
According to [[AGB Nielsen Philippines]]' Nationwide Urban Television Audience Measurement People in Television Homes, the pilot episode of ''Black Rider'' earned a 12.1% rating.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pilot episode ng ''Black Rider'', kumasa ba sa ''Batang Quiapo''? |url=https://www.pep.ph/pepalerts/pep-troika/176977/black-rider-batang-quiapo-ratings-a4118-20231107 |access-date=November 8, 2023 |website=PEP |language=en}}</ref> The final episode scored a 15.6% rating.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pep.ph/pepalerts/pep-troika/182034/black-rider-finale-ratings-a4118-20240729 |title=''Black Rider'' finale episode, nataasan ang ''Batang Quiapo'' sa ratings  |date=July 29, 2024 |website=PEP |access-date=July 30, 2024}}</ref>

'''''Light Bringer''''' is a 2023 science fiction novel by American author [[Pierce Brown]]; it is the third book of a tetralogy which continues the story of his ''[[Red Rising]]'' trilogy (2014–2016). ''Light Bringer'' takes place after the events of ''[[Dark Age (novel)|Dark Age]]'' (2019), as the survivors from Mercury make their way to Mars and the Solar Republic.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Light Bringer by Pierce Brown: 9780425285992 {{!}} PenguinRandomHouse.com: Books |url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/545689/light-bringer-by-pierce-brown/ |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=PenguinRandomhouse.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Plot ==
<!-- TRY TO KEEP THIS PLOT SUMMARY TO WITHIN 700 WORDS PER WP:PLOTSUM -->
After the Republic loses [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]] to the Society, Darrow and his remaining soldiers hide on the 'trash moon' Marcher-1682 for eight months. After fuel is obtained, Darrow's soldiers return to [[Mars]]. Darrow, Cassius and Aurae attempt to rescue Sevro on [[Venus]] from Apollonius, but Sevro has already escaped, and Apollonius captures Darrow and Cassius. Apollonius duels and defeats Darrow, but Sevro rescues Darrow and Cassius. They flee Venus with Aurae, who asks Sevro to lead the Rim's Daughters of Athena.

Lysander is celebrated as Mercury's ruler, but Atalantia orders him to [[Earth]] and captures his mentor, Glirastes. Atalantia intends for Lysander to lead an assault on [[Moon|Luna]], but Lysander defies her, convincing the Society to attack Mars, ensuring Gilrastes' death by Atalantia. Lysander reveals his knowledge of Atalantia killing his parents. Ajax chooses Lysander over Atalantia, who besieges Luna.

While the Society and the Republic's fleets battle over Mars, the Society attacks [[Phobos (moon)|Phobos]], gaining a foothold. Virginia jailbreaks Valdir to escape Apollonius. Ajax is killed by Victra and Thraxa. Lysander [[parley]]s with Virginia, who relinquishes Phobos for her forces' safe passage to Mars and a prisoner swap for Kavax and Cicero. Lysander is poisoned by his bodyguard Rhone, who has allied with Atlas. Virginia orders Darrow to bypass the besieged Mars to retrieve Quicksilver's supposed fleet.

At Atlas' behest, Fá's Obsidians and Ascomanni attack the [[moons of Jupiter]], drawing the Dominion's forces from Mars; a recuperating Lysander follows. As revenge against the Dominion's past rebellion, Atlas and Fá decimate the Dominion's forces at [[Kalyke]], killing Dido and Helios. Lysander is captured but evacuates Diomedes. Atlas plans for Lysander to save the Rim from Fá; Lysander agrees. Fá enslaves [[Io (moon)|Io]], bombs [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]], then invades [[Europa (moon)|Europa]].

Lyria, searching for answers in the Rim, is rescued by Matteo from Dominion Golds. Lyria chooses her memories over the Psyche tool's enhancement; Matteo extracts it and Lyria destroys it. Darrow's group find Quicksilver, Matteo and Lyria. Quicksilver reveals that his fleet was transformed into a [[generation ship]] containing non-Color children to escape the [[Solar System]]. Darrow decides to travel to the Rim for the Daughters' fleet; Lyria joins Darrow's group as a stowaway. Cassius trains Darrow in swordsmanship. Lyria reveals Ulysses' death to Sevro.

At Kalyke, Darrow's group rescue Diomedes. On Io, they contact the Daughters, who repel the Obsidians' attack on Darrow and Cassius. The Obsidian Sigurd surrenders. Darrow's group enters the Daughters' base on Europa. Athena puts Darrow and Diomedes on trial, given Darrow's betrayal of the Rim's Sons of Ares to be killed by Romulus, while Diomedes admits the failure of the Dominion's rule. Sevro intervenes to have Darrow, Diomedes and Cassius spared to join the Daughters' fight against Fá.

Sigurd helps bring Lyria to Volga, who betrays Lyria to Fá. On Fá's orders, Volga kills Sigurd and then goes to kill Lyria, but Darrow interrupts, challenging Fá to a duel. Darrow defeats Fá after evolving his swordfighting style mid-fight. Fá implores the Obsidian braves and the Ascommani to kill Darrow and flees. Darrow corners Fá, who confesses before the Obsidians that he serves Atlas. Darrow states that because Fá serves Gold, he can be no true king. Thus, Darrow lets Volga, Fá's biological granddaughter, decide; she kills Fá. Darrow arranges an election for Obsidian leadership which Volga wins, thus becoming Queen of the Obsidian.

Lysander's forces arrive and massacre the Ascomanni, broadcasting Io's liberation. Diomedes has himself, Lysander and Darrow meet; they reluctantly unite against Atalantia and Atlas. Later, Cassius meets Lysander to propose killing Atlas, who returns after retrieving the biological weapon ''Eidmi'', which can eliminate any selected Color on any planet. Lysander and Cassius fight and kill Rhone and Atlas, though Atlas reveals that Lysander is using Cassius to obtain ''Eidmi''. Cassius wants ''Eidmi'' destroyed but Lysander wants to control it. Cassius attacks; Lysander kills him.

Gaia captures Darrow, intent on maintaining the Golds' hierarchy and vowing to kill Darrow. Diomedes demands Gaia abandon the hierarchy or kill him; Gaia relents. The Dominion elect as leader Diomedes, who allies with the Republic, with Gaia's support. Lysander pretends that Cassius tried to assassinate him, and uses this pretext to devastate Io, destroying the Rim's crops while stealing crops for the Core. Lysander's forces flee for the Core; he ponders using ''Eidmi'' on Red or Gold. The Republic, the Dominion, the Daughters and the Obsidians enter an uneasy alliance; their forces leave for Mars.
<!-- TRY TO KEEP THIS PLOT SUMMARY TO WITHIN 700 WORDS PER WP:PLOTSUM -->

== Reception ==
The week of August 7, 2023, ''Light Bringer'' landed on ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''<nowiki/>'s best seller lists in second place for fiction and fifth overall.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Juris |first=Carolyn |date=2023-08-04 |title=This Week's Bestsellers: August 7, 2023 |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/92926-this-week-s-bestsellers-august-7-2023.html |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Publishers Weekly]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week, it ranked second  on the [[The New York Times Best Seller list|New York Times Best Seller List]] for Hardcover Fiction<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hardcover Fiction Books - Best Sellers - Books - July 16, 2023 - The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/books/best-sellers/2023/07/16/hardcover-fiction/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and [[USA Today]]'s Best-selling Booklist for fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best-selling Booklist |url=https://www.usatoday.com/booklist/booklist |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

According to Brian Kitson of ''The Cosmic Circus,'' if readers are "looking for another well-written science-fiction/fantasy novel on audio, then ''Light Bringer'' should definitely be on [their] list".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kitson |first=Brian |date=2023-09-13 |title=Audiobook Review: 'Light Bringer' by Pierce Brown |url=https://thecosmiccircus.com/audiobook-review-light-bringer-a-red-rising-novel-by-pierce-brown/ |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=The Cosmic Circus |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Booklist]]'' also reviewed the novel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2023 |title=Light Bringer |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/Light-Bringer/pid=9780867 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref>

In 2023, ''Light Bringer'' placed second in the [[Goodreads Choice Awards|Goodreads Choice Award]] for Science Fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcing the Goodreads Choice Winner in Best Science Fiction! |url=https://www.goodreads.com/choiceawards/best-science-fiction-books-2023 |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Goodreads}}</ref> [[Barnes & Noble]] named it one of the best science fiction books of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-10-11 |title=Barnes & Noble Best Books of the Year 2023 |url=https://locusmag.com/2023/10/barnes-noble-best-books-of-the-year-2023/ |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Locus Online]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

''Light Bringer'' takes place after the events of ''[[Dark Age (novel)|Dark Age]]'' (2019), as the survivors from Mercury make their way to Mars and the Solar Republic.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Light Bringer by Pierce Brown: 9780425285992 {{!}} PenguinRandomHouse.com: Books |url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/545689/light-bringer-by-pierce-brown/ |access-date=2024-07-09 |website=PenguinRandomhouse.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Plot ==
<!-- TRY TO KEEP THIS PLOT SUMMARY TO WITHIN 700 WORDS PER WP:PLOTSUM -->
Eight months after the Republic loses [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]] to the Society, Darrow and his remaining soldiers hide on the 'trash moon' Marcher-1682. After obtaining fuel, Darrow's soldiers return to [[Mars]] while Darrow, Cassius and Aurae sail to rescue Sevro on [[Venus]] from Apollonius. However, Sevro has already escaped, and Apollonius captures Darrow and Cassius. Apollonius duels and defeats Darrow, but Sevro bombs the dockyards and rescues Darrow and Cassius. They flee Venus with Aurae, who asks Sevro to lead the Rim's Daughters of Athena, Fitchner's contingency should the Sons of Ares fail.

Lysander is celebrated as Mercury's savior, but still dreams of uniting the system's Golds as Sovereign. He transforms the ''Morning Star'' into the ''Lightbringer''. Atalantia discovers the ships and soldiers he had been funneling to Apollonius and orders him to attend her summit on [[Earth]]. She intends for Lysander to lead an assault to reclaim [[Moon|Luna]], but Lysander defies her, preaching that Gold has lost its way and to reclaim their role as shepherds of the colors, must defeat the Republic on Mars. Many of the Golds rally to him, including Cicero and Julia, but Atalantia kills Lysander's mentor Glirastes in retribution. Lysander reveals to Atalantia he knows of her role in his parents death and Ajax chooses Lysander over Atalantia. She remains to besiege Luna.

While the Society and the Republic's fleets battle in orbit over Mars, Lysander attacks [[Phobos (moon)|Phobos]]. Thousands are killed in battle, both Kavax and Cicero are gravely injured, and Virginia is forced to retreat deeper into the moon. She releases Valdir from prison to escape Apollonius. Ajax is killed by Victra and Thraxa. Lysander [[parley]]s with Virginia, who relinquishes Phobos' dockyards in exchange for her forces' safe passage to Mars and a prisoner swap of Kavax for Cicero. At a celebration, Lysander informs Diomedes of his intent to launch an Iron Rain on Mars within days, but is poisoned and falls into a coma. Darrow contacts Virginia who orders him to avoid the siege of Mars in favor of retrieving Quicksilver's supposed fleet from the [[Asteroid belt|Asteroid Belt]], whose location was discovered by Lyria.

Lyria, searching for answers about Figment's parasite in the Belt, is rescued from a cohort of Rim Golds by Matteo. He offers her a choice to repair the parasite, gaining significant physical and cognitive enhancements, at the cost of her memories. Lyria chooses to have it removed. Darrow's group find Quicksilver, Matteo and Lyria. Quicksilver reveals that he has not built a fleet but an interstellar [[generation ship]] containing non-Color ''[[Human|Homo sapiens]]'' children. He has charted the ship to escape the [[Solar System]] as insurance for mankind, believing the war will eventually consume all the worlds. Quicksilver outfits Darrow to travel to the Rim and recruit the Daughter's fleet, Lyria joins as a stowaway, and Sevro joins after Lyria reveals Ulysses' death. Cassius trains Darrow in his style of swordsmanship.

Volsung Fá's Volk Obsidians and Ascomanni tribes attack the [[moons of Jupiter]], drawing the Dominion's forces from Mars; a recuperating Lysander joins Diomedes on his flagship. At the moon [[Kalyke]], Helios boards the ''Dustmaker'', but it is revealed to be Atlas carved in his likeness. In vengeance for the Rim's two rebellions against the Society, Atlas decimates the Rim's fleet, killing Dido and Helios. Lysander is captured but helps Diomedes escape. Lysander's Dux, Rhone, is revealed to be behind his poisoning and has allied with Atlas. Atlas, the puppet master behind Fá, arranges for Lysander to "save" the Rim from the Obsidians, intending to have Lysander, not Atalantia, lead the Society into a new era of peace. To spare civilian lives, Lysander agrees to perpetuate the lie of Fá. Fá razes [[Io (moon)|Io]] and enslaves its inhabitants, bombs [[Callisto (moon)|Callisto]], then invades [[Europa (moon)|Europa]]. Volga leads the Obsidians at his side.

Darrow's group rescue Diomedes from the wreckage at Kalyke, taking him captive. On Io, they contact the Daughters, who rescue enslaved Ionians from the Obsidians with Darrow and Cassius. Darrow's group enters the Daughters' base below the oceans of Europa where Athena puts Darrow and Diomedes on trial for Darrow's betrayal of the Rim's Sons of Ares to Romulus and for Diomedes' failure to protect the lowColors of Rim society. Sevro intervenes to have Darrow, Diomedes and Cassius spared to join the Daughters' fight against Fá.

Lyria is smuggled to Volga, who reveals she is now willingly working with Fá and seeking to form an Obsidian homeland. However, when Fá orders Volga to kill Lyria, she cannot. Darrow interrupts, challenging Fá to a duel. Darrow publicly defeats Fá, who tries to flee, but is cornered and confesses to serving Atlas before the Obsidians. Darrow allows Volga to decide Fá's fate and she kills him. Darrow arranges an election for Obsidian leadership and Volga becomes Queen of the Obsidians.

Lysander's forces arrive and massacre the Ascomanni in the Garter, broadcasting Io's liberation. Diomedes organizes a meeting between Lysander and Darrow, urging them to form an alliance against the Core Golds and establish peace built on compromise. Darrow is willing, but Lysander is unsure. As Lysander considers the offer on the ''Lightbringer'', Cassius arrives and proposes that they kill Atlas, freeing Lysander from his schemes. Atlas returns after retrieving a biological weapon ''Eidmi'', which can eliminate any selected Color on any planet. Lysander and Cassius fight and kill Rhone and Atlas, though with his final words Atlas reveals that Lysander is using Cassius to obtain ''Eidmi''. Cassius wants ''Eidmi'' destroyed but Lysander wants to control it, seeing it as the only way to ensure peace and end the war. When Cassius tries to take it by force, Lysander kills him.

Gaia captures Darrow, intent on maintaining Atlas' lie of Volsung Fá and make peace with Atalantia to preserve the Gold hierarchy. However, Diomedes demands Gaia abandon the hierarchy or kill him and Gaia relents. The Moon Lords elect Diomedes as their leader and Darrow publicly presents the head of Fá and apologizes for his destruction of the Ganymede dockyards. With Gaia's support, the Moon Lords are prepared to ally with the Republic and Lysander against Atalantia and Atlas, but Lysander fails to show at the summit. He contacts them remotely, lying that Cassius attempted to assassinate him and uses this as pretext to devastate Io, destroying the Rim's capacity to feed itself and enriching the Core. As the fleets of Athena and Volga converge on Io, Lysander's forces flee for the Core; he ponders using ''Eidmi'' on Red or Gold. The Republic, the Rim Dominion, the Daughters and the Volk enter an uneasy alliance and their combined forces leave for Mars.

== Reception ==
The week of August 7, 2023, ''Light Bringer'' landed on ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''<nowiki/>'s best seller lists in second place for fiction and fifth overall.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Juris |first=Carolyn |date=2023-08-04 |title=This Week's Bestsellers: August 7, 2023 |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/92926-this-week-s-bestsellers-august-7-2023.html |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Publishers Weekly]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week, it ranked second  on the [[The New York Times Best Seller list|New York Times Best Seller List]] for [[Hardcover]] Fiction<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hardcover Fiction Books - Best Sellers - Books - July 16, 2023 - The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/books/best-sellers/2023/07/16/hardcover-fiction/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and [[USA Today]]'s Best-selling Booklist for fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best-selling Booklist |url=https://www.usatoday.com/booklist/booklist |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

According to Brian Kitson of ''The Cosmic Circus,'' if readers are "looking for another well-written science-fiction/fantasy novel on audio, then ''Light Bringer'' should definitely be on [their] list".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kitson |first=Brian |date=2023-09-13 |title=Audiobook Review: 'Light Bringer' by Pierce Brown |url=https://thecosmiccircus.com/audiobook-review-light-bringer-a-red-rising-novel-by-pierce-brown/ |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=The Cosmic Circus |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Booklist]]'' also reviewed the novel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2023 |title=Light Bringer |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/Light-Bringer/pid=9780867 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref>

In 2023, ''Light Bringer'' placed second in the [[Goodreads Choice Awards|Goodreads Choice Award]] for Science Fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcing the Goodreads Choice Winner in Best Science Fiction! |url=https://www.goodreads.com/choiceawards/best-science-fiction-books-2023 |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Goodreads}}</ref> [[Barnes & Noble]] named it one of the best science fiction books of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-10-11 |title=Barnes & Noble Best Books of the Year 2023 |url=https://locusmag.com/2023/10/barnes-noble-best-books-of-the-year-2023/ |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Locus Online]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Lysander and Cassius fight and kill Rhone and Atlas, though with his final words Atlas reveals that Lysander is using Cassius to obtain ''Eidmi''. Cassius wants ''Eidmi'' destroyed but Lysander wants to control it, seeing it as the only way to ensure peace and end the war. When Cassius tries to take it by force, Lysander kills him.

Gaia captures Darrow, intent on maintaining Atlas' lie of Volsung Fá and make peace with Atalantia to preserve the Gold hierarchy. However, Diomedes demands Gaia abandon the hierarchy or kill him and Gaia relents. The Moon Lords elect Diomedes as their leader and Darrow publicly presents the head of Fá and apologizes for his destruction of the Ganymede dockyards. With Gaia's support, the Moon Lords are prepared to ally with the Republic and Lysander against Atalantia and Atlas, but Lysander fails to show at the summit. He contacts them remotely, lying that Cassius attempted to assassinate him and uses this as pretext to devastate Io, destroying the Rim's capacity to feed itself and enriching the Core. As the fleets of Athena and Volga converge on Io, Lysander's forces flee for the Core; he ponders using ''Eidmi'' on Red or Gold. The Republic, the Rim Dominion, the Daughters and the Volk enter an uneasy alliance and their combined forces leave for Mars.

== Reception ==
The week of August 7, 2023, ''Light Bringer'' landed on ''[[Publishers Weekly]]''<nowiki/>'s best seller lists in second place for fiction and fifth overall.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Juris |first=Carolyn |date=2023-08-04 |title=This Week's Bestsellers: August 7, 2023 |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/pw/by-topic/industry-news/bookselling/article/92926-this-week-s-bestsellers-august-7-2023.html |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=[[Publishers Weekly]] |language=en}}</ref> The following week, it ranked second  on the [[The New York Times Best Seller list|New York Times Best Seller List]] for [[Hardcover]] Fiction<ref>{{Cite news |title=Hardcover Fiction Books - Best Sellers - Books - July 16, 2023 - The New York Times |url=https://www.nytimes.com/books/best-sellers/2023/07/16/hardcover-fiction/ |access-date=2024-07-24 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> and [[USA Today]]'s Best-selling Booklist for fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Best-selling Booklist |url=https://www.usatoday.com/booklist/booklist |access-date=2024-07-24 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref>

According to Brian Kitson of ''The Cosmic Circus,'' if readers are "looking for another well-written science-fiction/fantasy novel on audio, then ''Light Bringer'' should definitely be on [their] list".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kitson |first=Brian |date=2023-09-13 |title=Audiobook Review: 'Light Bringer' by Pierce Brown |url=https://thecosmiccircus.com/audiobook-review-light-bringer-a-red-rising-novel-by-pierce-brown/ |access-date=2024-07-29 |website=The Cosmic Circus |language=en-US}}</ref> ''[[Booklist]]'' also reviewed the novel.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 2023 |title=Light Bringer |url=https://www.booklistonline.com/Light-Bringer/pid=9780867 |url-access=subscription |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Booklist]]}}</ref>

In 2023, ''Light Bringer'' placed second in the [[Goodreads Choice Awards|Goodreads Choice Award]] for Science Fiction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcing the Goodreads Choice Winner in Best Science Fiction! |url=https://www.goodreads.com/choiceawards/best-science-fiction-books-2023 |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Goodreads}}</ref> [[Barnes & Noble]] named it one of the best science fiction books of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-10-11 |title=Barnes & Noble Best Books of the Year 2023 |url=https://locusmag.com/2023/10/barnes-noble-best-books-of-the-year-2023/ |access-date=2024-08-09 |website=[[Locus Online]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

She had a younger brother, who died of [[pancreatic cancer]] at the age of two.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/08/felice-herrig-first-childrens-book-ufc-252-injury-return-women-mma|title=Felice Herrig's first children's book is out the week of her UFC 252 return|date=August 11, 2020|publisher=mmajunkie.com}} Herrig began her career practicing kickboxing and Muay Thai before transitioning to MMA in 2009.{{cite news|title=Buffalo Grove fighter Felice Herrig gets her shot on reality TV|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/07/03/fighter-returns-to-reality-tv/|first=Mike|last=Helfgot|date=2009-07-03|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=2011-10-11}} Herrig graduated from [[Buffalo Grove High School]] in 2003.{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/07/03/fighter-returns-to-reality-tv/|title = Fighter returns to reality TV}} ==Kickboxing career== [[File:Felice Herrig fighting at Muay Thai Mayhem XIV (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Herrig in a match at Muay Thai Mayhem XIV in New York City on June 16, 2009]] Prior to Herrig's move to mixed martial arts, she held a professional kickboxing record of 23–5.{{cite web|url=http://www.ufc.com/fighter/Felice-Herrig|title=Felice Herrig - Official UFC Fighter Profile|publisher=UFC.com|access-date=April 19, 2015}} She was ranked as high as number 2 in the World in the IKF [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Pro Women's Muay Thai Bantamweight Division. As a pro kickboxer, Herrig won the [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Pro Muay Thai United States Bantamweight Title. She won the title on November 15, 2008, in Chicago, Illinois, US, when she defeated Katie Meehan by unanimous decision (49-46, 48–47, 49–46). As an amateur, she was a two-time [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Open Tournament Champion. On August 21, 2005, Herrig became the 2005 IKF North American Classic Amateur Full Contact Rules Bantamweight Tournament Champion when she defeated Terri French of Little Rock, Arkansas, US, by unanimous decision 30–27 on all 3 judges cards. On July 30, 2006, Herrig defended her IKF Tournament Title at the 2006 IKF World Classic when she defeated Stacy Chung of Thunder Bay, Ontario, Canada by unanimous decision 29–28 on all 3 judges cards. She has also competed in the [[World Combat League]] with the St. Louis Enforcers.{{cite web|url=http://www.mouthpiecesports.com/media/mma-fighter-felice-herrig-is-bantering-with-brian-dryfhout-22562/|title=MMA Fighter Felice Herrig is Bantering with Brian Dryfhout|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=MouthpieceSports.com|date=2009-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091218085108/http://www.mouthpiecesports.com/media/mma-fighter-felice-herrig-is-bantering-with-brian-dryfhout-22562/|archive-date=2009-12-18|url-status=dead}} ==Mixed martial arts career== [[File:VCJCS 2019 USO Tour 190331-D-SW162-1254 (40544642293).jpg|thumb|upright=1.7|left| Felice Herrig at Bagram Airfield, Afghanistan; the second stop on the annual Vice Chairman's USO Tour, March 31, 2019.]] Herrig appeared on [[Fight Girls]] in 2007 on the [[Oxygen (TV channel)|Oxygen]] and won her fight in [[Thailand]] against a champion Thai fighter.{{cite web|url=http://fighthype.com/pages/content5394.html|title=Felice Herrig: "Girls Want Nothing To Do With My Standup"|access-date=2009-08-19|publisher=FightHype.com|date=2009-08-06}} She was later scheduled to appear on another reality show about women's MMA called the [[Ultimate Women Challenge]]. Herrig faced Iman Achhal at UWC: Man "O" War on February 21, 2009, in her MMA debut. She lost the fight by split decision.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/articles/Easton-Captures-UWC-Gold-Patterson-Victorious-16298|title=Easton Captures UWC Gold; Patterson Victorious|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=Sherdog.com|date=2009-02-22}} She faced Michele Gutierrez at Unconquered 1: November Reign on November 20, 2009, and won the fight by armbar submission in the second round.{{cite web|url=http://chicagosmma.com/2009/12/highlights-of-felice-herrigs-first-mma-victory/|title=Highlights of Felice Herrig's First MMA Victory|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=ChicagosMMA.com|date=2009-12-03}} Herrig faced [[Jessica Rakoczy]] at [[Bellator 14]] on April 15, 2010.{{cite web |url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Askren-Thomas-Cleared-for-Bellator-14-23877|title=Askren, Thomas Cleared for Bellator 14|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=Sherdog.com|date=2010-04-14}} She won the fight via split decision.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mma/blog/cagewriter/post/Herrig-ekes-out-a-split-decision-while-Curran-lo?urn=mma%2C234604|title=Herrig ekes out a split decision while Curran loses in UD at Bellator|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=YAHOO! Sports|date=2010-04-15}} Herrig faced Amanda LaVoy at XFO 37 on December 4, 2010. She won the fight via armbar submission in the first round.{{cite web|url=http://www.ultmma.com/news/index.php?itemid=1365|title=XFO 37 results – Jeff Curran picks up win & Felice Herrig vs. Amanda LaVoy fight video|access-date=2010-12-06|publisher=ULTMMA.com|date=2010-12-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926155124/http://www.ultmma.com/news/index.php?itemid=1365|archive-date=2015-09-26|url-status=dead}} On January 14, 2011, Herrig faced [[Barb Honchak]] at Hoosier Fight Club 6: New Years Nemesis in Valparaiso, Indiana. She had a younger brother, who died of [[pancreatic cancer]] at the age of two.{{cite web|url=https://mmajunkie.usatoday.com/2020/08/felice-herrig-first-childrens-book-ufc-252-injury-return-women-mma|title=Felice Herrig's first children's book is out the week of her UFC 252 return|date=August 11, 2020|publisher=mmajunkie.com}} Herrig began her career practicing kickboxing and Muay Thai before transitioning to MMA in 2009.{{cite news|title=Buffalo Grove fighter Felice Herrig gets her shot on reality TV|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/07/03/fighter-returns-to-reality-tv/|first=Mike|last=Helfgot|date=2009-07-03|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|access-date=2011-10-11}} Herrig graduated from [[Buffalo Grove High School]] in 2003.{{Cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2009/07/03/fighter-returns-to-reality-tv/|title = Fighter returns to reality TV}} ==Kickboxing career== [[File:Felice Herrig fighting at Muay Thai Mayhem XIV (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Herrig in a match at Muay Thai Mayhem XIV in New York City on June 16, 2009]] Prior to Herrig's move to mixed martial arts, she held a professional kickboxing record of 23–5.{{cite web|url=http://www.ufc.com/fighter/Felice-Herrig|title=Felice Herrig - Official UFC Fighter Profile|publisher=UFC.com|access-date=April 19, 2015}} She was ranked as high as number 2 in the World in the IKF [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Pro Women's Muay Thai Bantamweight Division. As a pro kickboxer, Herrig won the [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Pro Muay Thai United States Bantamweight Title. She won the title on November 15, 2008, in Chicago, Illinois, US, when she defeated Katie Meehan by unanimous decision (49-46, 48–47, 49–46). As an amateur, she was a two-time [[International Kickboxing Federation]] Open Tournament Champion. On August 21, 2005, Herrig became the 2005 IKF North American Classic Amateur Full Contact Rules Bantamweight Tournament Champion when she defeated Terri French of Little Rock, Arkansas, US, by unanimous decision 30–27 on all 3 judges cards. On July 30, 2006, Herrig defended her IKF Tournament Title at the 2006 IKF World Classic when she defeated Stacy Chung of Thunder Bay, Ontario, Canada by unanimous decision 29–28 on all 3 judges cards. She has also competed in the [[World Combat League]] with the St. Louis Enforcers.{{cite web|url=http://www.mouthpiecesports.com/media/mma-fighter-felice-herrig-is-bantering-with-brian-dryfhout-22562/|title=MMA Fighter Felice Herrig is Bantering with Brian Dryfhout|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=MouthpieceSports.com|date=2009-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091218085108/http://www.mouthpiecesports.com/media/mma-fighter-felice-herrig-is-bantering-with-brian-dryfhout-22562/|archive-date=2009-12-18|url-status=dead}} ==Mixed martial arts career== [[File:VCJCS 2019 USO Tour 190331-D-SW162-1254 (40544642293).jpg|thumb|upright=1.7|left| Felice Herrig at Bagram Airfield, Afghanistan; the second stop on the annual Vice Chairman's USO Tour, March 31, 2019.]] Herrig appeared on [[Fight Girls]] in 2007 on the [[Oxygen (TV channel)|Oxygen]] and won her fight in [[Thailand]] against a champion Thai fighter.{{cite web|url=http://fighthype.com/pages/content5394.html|title=Felice Herrig: "Girls Want Nothing To Do With My Standup"|access-date=2009-08-19|publisher=FightHype.com|date=2009-08-06}} She was later scheduled to appear on another reality show about women's MMA called the [[Ultimate Women Challenge]]. Herrig faced Iman Achhal at UWC: Man "O" War on February 21, 2009, in her MMA debut. She lost the fight by split decision.{{cite web|url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/articles/Easton-Captures-UWC-Gold-Patterson-Victorious-16298|title=Easton Captures UWC Gold; Patterson Victorious|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=Sherdog.com|date=2009-02-22}} She faced Michele Gutierrez at Unconquered 1: November Reign on November 20, 2009, and won the fight by armbar submission in the second round.{{cite web|url=http://chicagosmma.com/2009/12/highlights-of-felice-herrigs-first-mma-victory/|title=Highlights of Felice Herrig's First MMA Victory|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=ChicagosMMA.com|date=2009-12-03}} Herrig faced [[Jessica Rakoczy]] at [[Bellator 14]] on April 15, 2010.{{cite web |url=http://www.sherdog.com/news/news/Askren-Thomas-Cleared-for-Bellator-14-23877|title=Askren, Thomas Cleared for Bellator 14|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=Sherdog.com|date=2010-04-14}} She won the fight via split decision.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/mma/blog/cagewriter/post/Herrig-ekes-out-a-split-decision-while-Curran-lo?urn=mma%2C234604|title=Herrig ekes out a split decision while Curran loses in UD at Bellator|access-date=2010-04-16|publisher=YAHOO! Sports|date=2010-04-15}} Herrig faced Amanda LaVoy at XFO 37 on December 4, 2010. She won the fight via armbar submission in the first round.{{cite web|url=http://www.ultmma.com/news/index.php?itemid=1365|title=XFO 37 results – Jeff Curran picks up win & Felice Herrig vs. Amanda LaVoy fight video|access-date=2010-12-06|publisher=ULTMMA.com|date=2010-12-06|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926155124/http://www.ultmma.com/news/index.php?itemid=1365|archive-date=2015-09-26|url-status=dead}} On January 14, 2011, Herrig faced [[Barb Honchak]] at Hoosier Fight Club 6: New Years Nemesis in Valparaiso, Indiana. She won the fight by TKO in the first round.{{cite web|url=http://chicagosmma.com/2011/03/pulver-wins-despite-broken-foot/|title=Pulver Wins Despite Broken Foot|access-date=2011-03-06|publisher=ChicagosMMA.com|date=2011-03-06}} Herrig faced [[Nicdali Rivera-Calanoc]] at XFO 39 on May 13, 2011, at the Sears Centre in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. She defeated Vidonic by unanimous decision.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmarising.com/articles/2012/04/13/felice-herrig-defeats-patricia-vidonic-at-xfc-17-apocalypse/|title=Felice Herrig Defeats Patricia Season Seven#Bellator LXXXIV|Bellator 84]] on December 14, 2012.{{cite web|url=http://www.mmarising.com/news/2012/10/12/felice-herrig-vs-michele-gutierrez-rematch-added-to-bellator-84/|title=Felice [[Ohio State University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''Keith Faber''' (born January 19, 1966) is an American lawyer and politician from [[Ohio]]. A [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]], he has been [[Ohio State Auditor|State Auditor of Ohio]] since 2019. He was formerly a member of the [[Ohio House of Representatives]] (2001-2007), elected from the 84th district, and then a member of the [[Ohio State Senate]] (2007-2016), elected from the [[Ohio's 12th senatorial district|12th District]]. He was [[List of Presidents of the Ohio Senate|president of the Ohio Senate]] from 2013 to 2016. ==Life and career== [[File:Congressman Jim Jordan at Opening of Sidney Office.jpg|thumb|left|Opening of [[United States Congress|Congressman]] [[Jim Jordan]]'s [[Sidney, Ohio|Sidney]] office in 2007. From left-to-right: John Garmhausen, State Senator Keith Faber, State Representative John Adams, Mayor Frank J. Mariano, City of Sidney, City Councilman Steve Hamby, Doug Borchers, Congressman Jim Jordan]] With incumbent [[Jim Buchy]] unable to run for another term in the House in 2000, Faber sought to replace him. He faced a primary race with fellow Republican Terry Haworth, and won by about 1,300 votes.Blackwell, Kenneth [http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/RepOhHouseReps03072000.aspx 2000 primary election results] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627173002/http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/RepOhHouseReps03072000.aspx |date=2011-06-27 }} (2000-03-07) He defeated Democrat Bill Sell in the general election by about 14,000 votes.Blackwell, Kenneth [http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/OHHouseReps11072000.aspx 2000 general election results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627172935/http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/OHHouseReps11072000.aspx |date=2011-06-27 }} (2000-11-07) He won reelection in 2002, 2004, and 2006. When [[Jim Jordan]] vacated his state Senate seat after winning a seat in Congress, Faber was one of seven who sought to replace him, along with [[Derrick Seaver]], [[Gene Krebs]], Robert J. [[Ohio State University]] ([[Juris Doctor|JD]]) }} '''Keith Faber''' (born January 19, 1966) is an American lawyer and politician from [[Ohio]]. A [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]], he has been [[Ohio State Auditor|State Auditor of Ohio]] since 2019. He was formerly a member of the [[Ohio House of Representatives]] (2001-2007), elected from the 84th district, and then a member of the [[Ohio State Senate]] (2007-2016), elected from the [[Ohio's 12th senatorial district|12th District]]. He was [[List of Presidents of the Ohio Senate|president of the Ohio Senate]] from 2013 to 2016. ==Life and career== [[File:Congressman Jim Jordan at Opening of Sidney Office.jpg|thumb|left|Opening of [[United States Congress|Congressman]] [[Jim Jordan]]'s [[Sidney, Ohio|Sidney]] office in 2007. From left-to-right: John Garmhausen, State Senator Keith Faber, State Representative John Adams, Mayor Frank J. Mariano, City of Sidney, City Councilman Steve Hamby, Doug Borchers, Congressman Jim Jordan]] With incumbent [[Jim Buchy]] unable to run for another term in the House in 2000, Faber sought to replace him. He faced a primary race with fellow Republican Terry Haworth, and won by about 1,300 votes.Blackwell, Kenneth [http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/RepOhHouseReps03072000.aspx 2000 primary election results] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627173002/http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/RepOhHouseReps03072000.aspx |date=2011-06-27 }} (2000-03-07) He defeated Democrat Bill Sell in the general election by about 14,000 votes.Blackwell, Kenneth [http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/OHHouseReps11072000.aspx 2000 general election results] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110627172935/http://www.sos.state.oh.us/SOS/elections/electResultsMain/2000ElectionsResults/OHHouseReps11072000.aspx |date=2011-06-27 }} (2000-11-07) He won reelection in 2002, 2004, and 2006. When [[Jim Jordan]] vacated his state Senate seat after winning a seat in Congress, Faber was one of seven who sought to replace him, along with [[Derrick Seaver]], [[Gene Krebs]], Robert J. Luckey III, Toni Slusser, Vincent Foulk and Kreg Allison. Faber won the support of Senate Republicans, and took the seat in the Senate in February 2007. Soon after the appointment, Senate President [[Bill Harris (Ohio politician)|Bill Harris]] appointed Faber to the Senate Finance and Financial Institutions Committee. For the [[128th Ohio General Assembly|128th General Assembly]], Faber served as Senate majority floor leader, and in the [[129th Ohio General Assembly|129th General Assembly]], he served as president pro tempore, the second highest post in the Senate.{{cite web|url=http://www.urbanacitizen.com/main.asp?SectionID=3&SubSectionID=5&ArticleID=155625|title=News Archives - Urbana Daily Citizen|website=Urbana Daily Citizen|access-date=2010-12-23|archive-date=2011-07-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717173231/http://www.urbanacitizen.com/main.asp?SectionID=3&SubSectionID=5&ArticleID=155625|url-status=dead}} As President pro tempore, Faber was also vice chairman of the Senate Rules and Reference Committee.{{cite web|url=http://www.daytondailynews.com/news/ohio-news/areas-state-lawmakers-take-leadership-spots-1055779.html?cxtype=rss_ece_frontpage|title=Area's state lawmakers take leadership spots}} Faber won reelection to a second term in 2012, defeating Libertarian Paul Hinds with 79.07% of the vote.Husted, Jon [http://www2.sos.state.oh.us/pls/enrpublic/f?p=212:17:1619888371307304::NO::P17_OTC:SE 2012 general election results] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20121204180223/http://www2.sos.state.oh.us/pls/enrpublic/f?p=212:17:1619888371307304::NO::P17_OTC:SE |date=2012-12-04 }} (2012-11-06) Faber served as the [[List of Presidents of the Ohio Senate|94th President of the Ohio Senate]] throughout his last term in the upper chamber, before being ineligible to run again in 2016 due to term limits. In a 2016 survey by ''Columbus Monthly'' of Statehouse insiders ("lawmakers, legislative aides, lobbyists, journalists and Kasich administration officials"), Faber was rated "Most Ambitious," "Most Humorless," "Least Compassionate," "Most Arrogant," and "Most Aggressive Campaign Fundraiser."{{cite web|url=https://www.columbusmonthly.com/content/stories/2016/09/rating-the-legislators.html|title=Rating the Legislators|first=Dave|last=Ghose|date=September 23, 2016|access-date=September 12, 2021|archive-date=September 12, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912014330/https://www.columbusmonthly.com/content/stories/2016/09/rating-the-legislators.html|url-status=dead}} ==Ohio House of Representatives== In 2016, state Representative [[Jim Buchy]], who had returned to the House after Faber had succeeded him in 2000, again decided to retire, in what perhaps strategically opened up the seat for Faber, who himself was term-limited from his seat in the Senate, where he had served as the body's president since 2013. He easily won election, receiving over 83% of the vote against Democrat Ed Huff in the 2016 general election. {{cite web | title = Faber passes gavel; sworn in as state rep | date = 4 January 2017 | url = https://sidneydailynews.com/news/58813/faber-passes-gavel-sworn-in-as-state-rep | access-date = 2017-01-08 }} ==Auditor of State== [[File:Keith Faber 2018 rally.jpg|thumb|right|Faber speaking at a rally in 2018]] ===Campaign=== In February 2017, Faber announced his intention to run for Ohio Auditor of State. Ohio Speaker of the House [[Cliff Rosenberger]] considered running for the Republican nomination for auditor,{{cite web|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/State/2017/10/24/House-speaker-ponders-run-for-state-auditor.html|title=House speaker Rosenberger ponders run for Ohio auditor|date=24 October 2017}} but chose not to do so.Mary Kilpatrick, [https://apnews.com/article/ccbfafd5cfa94c7dbd8991cbe1c18128 House Speaker Cliff Rosenberger says he won' run for state auditor], Cleveland.com (October 30, 2017). He ran unopposed for the Republican nomination in the May 2018 primary.[https://www.ohiosos.gov/elections/election-results-and-data/2018-official-elections-results/ 2018 Official Election Results], Ohio Secretary of State. During his campaign, Faber emphasized performance audits to promote government efficiency.{{cite web|url=http://www.sent-trib.com/news/faber-campaigns-on-vigilance/article_f3dbf7d2-ba20-11e8-9e54-3be195442c1b.html|title=Faber campaigns on vigilance|author=Roger LaPointe|date=September 16, 2018|newspaper=Sentinel-Tribune|access-date=October 9, 2018|archive-date=September 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918112559/http://www.sent-trib.com/news/faber-campaigns-on-vigilance/article_f3dbf7d2-ba20-11e8-9e54-3be195442c1b.html|url-status=dead}} Faber faced former U.S. Representative [[Zack Space]], the Democratic nominee, in the 2018 campaign for state auditor.{{cite web|author=Julie Carr Smyth|url=https://www.apnews.com/65edb6b96438404b9ff436b11c520673|title=Tax penalty questions swirl in race for Ohio auditor|date=October 12, 2018|agency=Associated Press}} In October 2018, the [[Associated Press]] published an investigation revealed that Faber and his businesses incurred penalties for tax delinquencies between 2008 and 2015 across multiple properties and years and in two counties. Before Faber's tax payment history came to light, Faber had run digital ads attacking Space for his two tax penalties in 2005 and 2008. Both candidates cited administrative errors as the reason for the late payments. Space's campaign accused Faber of hypocrisy; Faber’s bookkeeper took responsibility for the delays. On November 6, 2018, Faber was elected State Auditor.{{Cite web |url=https://myfox28columbus.com/news/local/gop-state-rep-keith-faber-elected-as-ohio-auditor |title=GOP state Rep. Keith Faber elected as Ohio auditor |agency=Associated Press |website=WTTE |date=6 November 2018 |language=en-US |access-date=2018-11-07}} Faber received 49.66% of the vote, defeating Space, who received 46.28%. ===Tenure=== Faber was first inaugurated as auditor on January 12, 2019.[https://apnews.com/article/a3276d7c03604134a1bc1e63b94f4c30 Friday kicks off inaugurals for new Ohio officeholders], Associated Press (January 11, 2019). He was [https://ohiochannel.org/programs/program/inaugural-ceremonies-auditor-keith-faber-2023 inaugurated for a second term] on January 9, 2023, joined by his family and sworn in by newly elected chief justice of the Ohio Supreme Court Sharon Kennedy. ==Electoral history== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:95%" |+ Ohio Senate: Results 2008 to 2012 !|Year !SD !|Democrat !|Votes !|Pct ! During his campaign, Faber emphasized performance audits to promote government efficiency.{{cite web|url=http://www.sent-trib.com/news/faber-campaigns-on-vigilance/article_f3dbf7d2-ba20-11e8-9e54-3be195442c1b.html|title=Faber campaigns on vigilance|author=Roger LaPointe|date=September 16, 2018|newspaper=Sentinel-Tribune|access-date=October 9, 2018|archive-date=September 18, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180918112559/http://www.sent-trib.com/news/faber-campaigns-on-vigilance/article_f3dbf7d2-ba20-11e8-9e54-3be195442c1b.html|url-status=dead}} Faber faced former U.S. Representative [[Zack Space]], the Democratic nominee, in the 2018 campaign for state auditor.{{cite web|author=Julie Carr Smyth|url=https://www.apnews.com/65edb6b96438404b9ff436b11c520673|title=Tax penalty questions swirl in race for Ohio auditor|date=October 12, 2018|agency=Associated Press}} In October 2018, the [[Associated Press]] published an investigation revealed that Faber and his businesses incurred penalties for tax delinquencies between 2008 and 2015 across multiple properties and years and in two counties. Before Faber's tax payment history came to light, Faber had run digital ads attacking Space for his two tax penalties in 2005 and 2008. Both candidates cited administrative errors as the reason for the late payments. Space's campaign accused Faber of hypocrisy; Faber’s bookkeeper took responsibility for the delays. On November 6, 2018, Faber was elected State Auditor.{{Cite web |url=https://myfox28columbus.com/news/local/gop-state-rep-keith-faber-elected-as-ohio-auditor |title=GOP state Rep. Keith Faber elected as Ohio auditor |agency=Associated Press |website=WTTE |date=6 November 2018 |language=en-US |access-date=2018-11-07}} Faber received 49.66% of the vote, defeating Space, who received 46.28%. ===Tenure=== Faber was first inaugurated as auditor on January 12, 2019.[https://apnews.com/article/a3276d7c03604134a1bc1e63b94f4c30 Friday kicks off inaugurals for new Ohio officeholders], Associated Press (January 11, 2019). [[File:Albert J Goddard, William H Murphy, and George F Cotterill, ca 1920s (SEATTLE 4980).jpg|thumb|Goddard at left, circa 1920s, with fellow former City Council member William H. Murphy and former Seattle mayor [[George F. Cotterill]]]]

'''Albert J. Goddard''' (July 15, 1863 – April 20, 1958) was an American politician in the state of [[Washington (US state)|Washington]]. He served in the [[Washington House of Representatives]] from 1895 to 1897.<ref>{{cite web |title=State of Washington Members of the Legislature, 1889 {{endash}} 2011 |url=https://leg.wa.gov/History/Legislative/Documents/MembersOfLeg2011.pdf |website=Washington State Legislature |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220420082957/https://leg.wa.gov/History/Legislative/Documents/MembersOfLeg2011.pdf |archive-date=2022-04-20 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=nyp.33433015380482;view=1up;seq=98 |page=94 |title=Steel & Searl's legislative souvenir manual for 1895-1896: containing lists of members of all legislative sessions, territorial and state officers, state institutions and boards of government, ballots for United States senators, Senate and House committees and employees, Supreme and Superior Court judges, National Guard, federal officials, county officers, banks, post offices, census, vote, officers of organizations, and other information in relation to the state of Washington |website=babel.hathitrust.org |access-date=22 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210322215424/https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=nyp.33433015380482;view=1up;seq=98 |archive-date=22 March 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Goddard was born in Iowa in 1863. He graduated in 1884 from the Norton Scientific Academy in Wilton, Iowa. In 1888, he moved to the [[Washington Territory]] and with his brother Charles established Pacific Iron Works, a foundry in [[Fremont, Seattle|Fremont, Washington]], a small city that was annexed by [[Seattle]] in 1891. He was the mayor of Fremont before that annexation.<ref name=researchworks>{{cite web|url=https://researchworks.oclc.org/archivegrid/data/264741359|title=Albert J. Goddard scrapbooks, 1913-1937|access-date=2020-09-19}} [[OCLC]] finding aid.</ref>

Because of its location remote from the center of Seattle, Pacific Iron Works was the only Seattle-area foundry or machine shop to survive the [[Great Seattle Fire]] in June 1889.<ref name=Goddard-house>{{cite web|url=https://web6.seattle.gov/DPD/HistoricalSite/QueryResult.aspx?ID=719905663|title=Summary for 916 N 36th ST N / Parcel ID 1972201850|publisher=Seattle Department of Neighborhoods|access-date=2020-09-19}}</ref>

From 1892 to 1894, he was a member of the [[Seattle City Council]]<ref name=researchworks /> (a bicameral legislature at the time<ref name=Goddard-house />) and, in 1894 and 1895 served in the [[Washington House of Representatives]].<ref name=Goddard-house /> During the [[Klondike Gold Rush]], he and his wife Clara relocated to Alaska and ran a successful steamboat operation carrying prospectors to and from the [[Yukon Territory]] from 1897 to 1901.<ref name=researchworks /> With them to Alaska, they brought the materials to build sawmill and two steamboats, which were hauled on the Dead Horse Trail over [[White Pass]] to [[Skagway, Alaska|Skagway]]. The boat he named after himself, the ''[[A. J. Goddard]]'' and the ''F. H. Kilbourne'' were the first two steamboats to run the upper [[Yukon River]] from Skagway to [[Dawson City]].<ref name=Goddard-house /> After the Gold Rush they returned to Seattle.<ref name=researchworks />

He served again on the Seattle City Council from 1908 to 1915,<ref name=Goddard-house /><ref name=researchworks /> and ran unsuccessfully to return to the Council in 1931.<ref name=Goddard-house /> He was active in banking and as a building contractor, and was heavily involved in Gold Rush reunions.<ref name=researchworks />

The sternwheeler-utility boat ''A. J. Goddard'' sank in 1901 and was rediscovered largely intact in 2008. On board the boat were artifacts of the period such as a gramophone with contemporary recordings.

He is one of the most exciting prospects in baseball, and as of end of 2025, consider a top 5 prospect<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prospect Rankings 2025 |url=https://www.mlb.com/milb/prospects?msockid=30da8edb94f26408035a9ca89535656e/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=mlb.com |language=eg}}</ref> <ref>{{Cite web |title=Prospect The Board |url=https://www.fangraphs.com/prospects/the-board/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=fangraphs.com |language=eg}}</ref> <ref>{{Cite news |last=Law |first=Keith |date=July 24, 2025 |title=Top 60 MLB prospects: Kevin McGonigle, Max Clark top mid-2025 rankings |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6502957/2025/07/24/mlb-top-prospects-2025-kevin-mcgonigle/ |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=nytimes.com/athletic |language=eg}}</ref>. He has excellent ball-strike recognition, but his overall approach needs improvement, not unusual for a player the same age as US high school seniors. He’s extremely talented defender and projects to be plus defender (70) at [[shortstop]]. As he matures, he is expected to develop more power, potentially plus power (70). Speed is another aspect of his game, where he had 47 [[stolen bases]] in 2025.
